blocks.text: Condo buildings in Albion
Rydge (10640 248 Street) is marketed by its developer and presale sources as an Albion project, while its MLS listings classify it Thornhill MR.
Streets, schools and getting around Albion

items.t: The City publishes no boundary for the MLS sub-area as such — the Albion Area Plan's Schedule 1 map is the closest official boundary document.

Working geography: the east Maple Ridge growth area along Lougheed Highway around 240 Street, with residential corridors 240 Street, 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue, the Albion Fairgrounds/Sports Complex lands by the Fraser River, and farmland in South Albion. Nearby areas: Cottonwood and East Central to the west, Thornhill to the northeast, Kanaka Creek / North Maple Ridge ground to the north, and the Fraser River along the south edge.
Maple Ridge community medians: detached $1,131,000; attached $525,000, $432/sq ft, 94% sale-to-list, 49 days on market.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is no known apartment-condo building in Albion at all. The attached stock is townhouse complexes clustered on the 240 Street corridor at 101–104 Avenue — Albion Station (10151 240 Street), Ridgemont (24108 104 Avenue) and The Warwick (10392 240A Street) — beside the Albion Commercial Corner at 104 Avenue and 240 Street.
SD42 runs K–7 elementary and 8–12 secondary, with no middle-school tier. Note the live area page mis-states two of these addresses (c'usqunela and Kanaka Creek) — the Ministry figures above govern.

Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in the Town Centre to the west; the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs from Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place, and routes on the Haney Place diagram include the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791. West Coast Express: Port Haney Station, 22300 River Road, and Maple Meadows Station, 20010 Dunn Avenue, serve the west side of the city on weekdays between Waterfront and Mission City.

blocks.text: Good to know about Albion

items.t: All three complexes stand within a few blocks of one corner. Albion Station (10151 240 Street), Ridgemont (24108 104 Avenue) and The Warwick (10392 240A Street) all cluster at 104 Avenue / 240 Street, beside the Albion Commercial Corner and c'usqunela Elementary — complex-level comparables here are effectively a single-intersection market.

The fairgrounds are the area's event anchor. The City confirms the Albion Fairgrounds hosts events year-round (including Country Fest, the Caribbean Festival and the Home Show) and the Albion Sport Complex is home to Planet Ice and the Golden Ears Winter Club (curling) — event-weekend traffic on 240 Street and Jim Robson Way is part of living beside the 240/104 cluster.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Albion

items.t: Form B diligence (all four counted complexes are strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For The Warwick, first establish whether the unit is a developer sale or a resale, because the document route differs.
Lougheed Transit Corridor note: Verify any corridor claim for a specific property on the City's current document.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws.

blocks.text: Good to know about Albion

items.t: The Albion Area Plan update (Oct 28, 2025) plans family growth, not seniors housing — commercial nodes, walking/cycling links and farmland buffers, with added townhouse density contemplated along 248 Street in the North East Albion review; no age-restricted or seniors component is described in the plan material checked, which is why no 55+ supply is coming from the pipeline.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Albion matches at every level: the City of Maple Ridge lists the neighbourhood as Albion/Kanaka, and its Official Community Plan carries an Albion Area Plan as Chapter 10.2.
The working streets of the attached market are 240 Street north–south and 102 Avenue and 104 Avenue east–west, with Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side and the Fraser River beyond it.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Townhouse is a named plan designation in Albion, not just a housing form: the Albion Area Plan's Townhouse designation permits multi-unit housing forms in areas with access to major corridors, commercial areas and public amenities.

Cluster Residential is the second attached designation: it permits clustered ground-oriented multi-unit forms, including townhouse, courtyard and fourplex units, in environmentally sensitive areas where integrated site design is required.

In North East Albion, the plan states townhouses will consist primarily of two- to three-storey building forms, and encourages townhouse or strata developments to locate adjacent to Kanaka Creek Regional Park and sensitive streams for stewardship of the environmental buffer.

The built example is Kanaka Springs: developer Epic Homes describes it as a 70-acre masterplan community of townhomes and single-family homes, surrounded by over 20 acres of dedicated environmental space and linked to 1.2 kilometres of neighbourhood trail systems.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The plan steers strata townhouses to the park edge on purpose: North East Albion policy encourages townhouse or strata developments adjacent to Kanaka Creek Regional Park and sensitive streams, so creek-side complexes here carry riparian and buffer obligations a mid-block complex does not.
402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties.

Farmland interface is a plan rule, not a neighbour dispute: the October 28, 2025 Albion Area Plan update introduces buffers where urban development meets farmland, and Agricultural Land Reserve parcels sit in South Albion.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Kanaka Creek Regional Park runs along the area's north and west sides, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supporting chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout.
Quote school addresses from the district or the BC Ministry list, not from listing copy: Albion Elementary is 10031 240 Street and Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary is 10445 245 Street.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Kanaka Springs, 24951 112 Avenue area, developer Epic Homes: a 70-acre masterplan community of townhomes and single-family homes with a village hub of mixed-use commercial space and a neighbourhood park, a 1.2-acre future central community park, over 20 acres of dedicated environmental space and a future elementary school planned nearby.

Albion Area Plan update: Council adopted updates on October 28, 2025, adding walking and cycling connections, supporting local commercial nodes and adding farmland buffers. Status: plan adopted (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: The 746 Haney Place / Albion is the sub-area's named route, interlining with the 745 at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue.
The Golden Ears Bridge west of the city connects Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows to Langley and Surrey, the route Albion drivers use for Highway 1 access.

blocks.text: Albion, Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is a south-edge question: Albion fronts the Fraser River, the flood construction level is 6.7 metres geodetic, and which lots are affected is per-parcel on the City's flood maps.

Riparian land is a north-edge question: complexes beside Kanaka Creek Regional Park and its tributary streams sit next to protected watercourse corridors, and the plan's Cluster Residential designation exists precisely for environmentally sensitive ground.

Agricultural Land Reserve status for South Albion parcels is per-parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's mapping, and the 2025 plan update's farmland buffers apply where urban development meets that land.

blocks.text: Albion home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

29 townhomes sold in Albion with a median price of $745,000 (the middle half sold between $699,900 and $800,500), taking a median of 22 days to sell at 98.2% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $525 per square foot, a median year built of 2016 and a median strata fee of $318 a month.
